newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NOWA EUROPA DAILY TO MERGE WITH LEGAL PAPER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NOWA EUROPA DAILY TO MERGE WITH LEGAL PAPER.

text.p: Polish economic daily Nowa Europa will merge with a legal paper, Gazeta Prawna, this year to increase circulation and strengthen its position on the market, Nowa Europa's editor-in-chief said on Friday.
"We plan to create a new product to become more competitive," Roman Chocyk told Reuters, adding the new paper was likely to be launched within several months.
The working title of the new paper is Gazeta Prawno-Gospodarcza, or The Legal and Economic Gazette.

Nowa Europa, created in 1992, is now owned by an Italian company publishing business daily Il Sole 24 Ore, which holds a 51-percent stake in the Polish paper, and a domestic firm Infor, which publishes Gazeta Prawna.

Chocyk said the merger should allow the new title to reach a circulation of at least 90,000 copies daily, which is the number of copies sold by Gazeta Prawna, published twice a week and providing legal advice.
He said Nowa Europa, now published in some 45,000 copies and selling only half of them, was bringing losses.

Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted the owner of Infor, Ryszard Pienkowski, as saying the merger was meant to ready the two papers for coming competition from Swedish company Bonnier, which plans to launch a new business daily in Poland called Puls Biznesu (The Pulse of Business).
